title: Roguelike hack & slash: made with GPT image gen/Meshy/Cascadeur Claude writes basically all the code
author: Future-Chapter2065
selftext:
Solo project I made to play some coop roguelike with my friends, one melee class and one ranged. A little ARPG roguelike (yeah...)

  
Since this sub cares more about the how than the what, the art pipeline:

  
Drew the concept art myself. Stuff it into GPT image gen then Meshy to get them into 3D. Cascadeur for animation. ...Well I also used Meshy stock animations, mostly for the trash mobs.  
  
Heres the barbarians M1 combo chain and M2 charge.  
Its still a bit barebones, grind through 3 biomes and face the final boss.

replies.author: djmisterjon
replies.body:
This is a paradigm that hype many beginners: writing code and seeing it work. That is usually a single day of learning.

That is why programming is a discipline that requires logic, something LLMs do not possess. They can generate working code and keep iterating until no errors remain. However, beneath the surface, your architecture will be a mess, poorly wired, with strong coupling between every system, no design patterns at all, or worse, multiple design patterns tangled together.  
No respect for SOLID or cleancode...

You will get a result fast, which creates an appealing façade. But after a few months of piling on new tasks, reality will catch up with you very quickly.

The bias is that seeing a working result gives the impression that programming is simply about writing code until the linters stop reporting errors.

You may have an impressive building to showcase, but without a solid foundation and good practices, everything will collapse, taking your investors and clients down with it.

replies.author: djmisterjon
replies.body:
To begin with, simply using the term AI implies that you attribute a form of intelligence to these systems, even though that is not the case. They are simply highly sophisticated mathematical models on steroids, based on probabilities, with a \~*seed* used to introduce a bit of entropy (write the same thing, get a different answer). 

They work very well, but LLMs have no intellectual capacity and are not capable of reasoning. 

They only iterate over probabilities to find paths there your diff.  
You use your logic before work, LLMs iterate until the code works.
